contents.reason: This is a linear-operator solution, not a universal tensor in a Hopf algebra; the assigned B page has a stronger algebraic failure example.

contents.reason: This is a linear-operator solution only and supplies no quasitriangular Hopf-algebra tensor in the assigned item inventory.

contents.name: Exercise 32: ordered-basis q operator and quadratic relation
contents.reason: The quadratic relation and Hecke factorization are later type-A Hecke content; this page proves no quadratic relation.

contents.name: General T_ij action on chosen tensor positions
contents.reason: Only the three R legs and adjacent operators required here are defined; a general indexed operator calculus is unnecessary.

contents.name: Exercise 33: equivalence of checked and un-checked YBE

contents.reason: The Braid Groups category retains the presentation-to-representation theorem; this pair proves the local relations only.

contents.name: Componentwise tensor-product algebra multiplication preceding Definition 4.7
contents.support: The source supplies the componentwise product and unit; the item proves the unit-evaluation detection consequence explicitly.

contents.name: Definition 4.7: universal R-matrix and leg embeddings
Example 4.8: commutative bialgebra implies cocommutative coproduct
contents.reason: This implication is false: commutative multiplication does not force cocommutativity. The local example assumes cocommutativity explicitly.

contents.name: Exercise 34: centrality of the full twist
contents.reason: Centrality of R_21 R in the image of the coproduct is not needed by the claimed braiding or local-operator results.

contents.name: Exercise 35: Fourier R for a cyclic group algebra
contents.reason: The assigned finite-double example uses its own canonical dual-basis tensor and does not require this separate cyclic Fourier construction.

contents.name: Exercise 36: alternate universal R from R_21 inverse
contents.reason: The alternate R construction is not needed for the definition, braiding theorem, or specified examples.
